rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says a passive participle can mean an active agent, so mastūr means concealing; conversely fāʿil can be passive, as in māʾ dāfiq.
rows.anchor: وعن الأخفش أن " مفعول " ربما ورد بمعنى فاعل كميمون

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view treats mastūr as figurative attribution: what is truly concealed lies beyond the veil, not the veil itself.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم أن ذلك من الإسناد المجازي والمستور بحسب الحقيقة هو ما وراء الحجاب لا نفسه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view supplies an omitted phrase: the veil is one by which the Messenger is concealed.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم أنه من قبيل الحذف والإيصال وأصله حجابا مستورا به الرسول

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view understands the veil as concealed by further, multiple veils.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى حجابا مستورا بحجاب آخر أي بحجب متعدده

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view takes mastūr to mean that its being a veil is itself hidden, so they do not know they do not know.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى حجابا مستورا كونه حجابا بمعنى أنهم لا يدرون أنهم لا يدرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls the last three explanations the weakest interpretations.
rows.anchor: والثلاثه الأخيرة أسخف الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akinna is the plural of kinn, a covering that protects and hides; waqr is heaviness in hearing; nufūr is the regular plural of nāfir.
rows.anchor: الأكنه جمع كن بالكسر وهو على ما ذكره الراغب ما يحفظ فيه الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart-coverings and ear-heaviness explain the prior veil: they cannot hear the Qurʾān receptively or understand it with belief, as requital for disbelief and disobedience.
rows.anchor: فهم لا يسمعون القرآن سمع قبول ولا يفقهونه فقه إيمان وتصديق كل ذلك مجازاة لهم بما كفروا وفسقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the Lord alone means affirming divine unity and denying any partner; they turn away in aversion.
rows.anchor: أي على نعت التوحيد ونفى الشريك ولوا على أدبارهم نافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwā is a verbal noun used of singular, dual, plural, masculine, or feminine subjects, with an unchanged form.
rows.anchor: النجوى مصدر ولذا يوصف به الواحد والمثنى والمجموع والمذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse evidences the preceding account: God knows the ears listening and hearts whispering; as their creator, His account of their coverings and deafness is true.
rows.anchor: والآية بمنزلة الحجة على ما ذكر في الآية السابقة أنه جعل على قلوبهم أكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They secretly came to hear the Prophet to avoid blame, then reproached one another in whispers lest he and the believers notice them; this supports the reported occasions of revelation.
rows.anchor: كانوا لا يأتونه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لاستماع القرآن علنا حذرا من اللائمة وإنما يأتونه متسترين مستخفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whisperers called the Prophet bewitched, showing that they had not understood the truth.
rows.anchor: وهذا تصديق أنهم لم يفقهوا الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathal means description and striking examples means describing through attributes; their distorted comparisons show there is no hope they will believe.
rows.anchor: المثل بمعنى الوصف، وضرب الأمثال التوصيف بالصفات ومعنى الآية ظاهر

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines rufāt as anything broken and decayed, with forms such as ḥuṭām, duqāq, and turāb for crushed things.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع الرفات ما تكسر وبلي من كل شيء

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines rufāt as anything pounded so thoroughly that it is pulverized.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد كل شيء مدقوق مبالغ في دقه حتى انسحق فهو رفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reject resurrection, although the Qurʾān establishes it through revelation and reason and describes it elsewhere as beyond doubt; their only argument is that it seems unlikely.
rows.anchor: وليس لهم حجة على نفيه غير أنهم استبعدوه استبعادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their presumption that death annihilates a person makes return from decayed bones and dust seem remote; God answers by recalling absolute power and the first creation.
rows.anchor: ومن أعظم ما يزين في قلوبهم هذا الاستبعاد زعمهم أن الموت فناء للإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to become stone, iron, or something still harder to imagine returning to human form is a coercive challenge answering their objection from decayed bones.
rows.anchor: فأمر سبحانه نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يأمرهم أمر تسخير أن يكونوا حجارة أو حديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever form they take, nothing is difficult for divine omnipotence to recreate, including stone, iron, or anything else they regard as harder to transform.
rows.anchor: فإن الله سيعيد إليهم خلقهم الأول ويبعثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they ask who will restore them to human form, the answer is the one who first created them when they were nothing, removing any basis for doubt.
rows.anchor: وهو فطره إياهم أول مرة ولم يكونوا شيئا وقل يعيدكم الذي خلقكم أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Creator the one who first formed them demonstrates possibility and removes improbability by presenting a familiar precedent.
rows.anchor: إثبات الإمكان ورفع الاستبعاد بإراءة المثل

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines inghāḍ as moving the head toward someone as if in amazement.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الإنغاض تحريك الرأس نحو الغير كالمتعجب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They shake their heads in mockery and contempt after hearing the proof; the time of resurrection is unknown except to God, though revelation identifies its character.
rows.anchor: تحريك المستهزئ المستخف بك المستهين له ويقولون متى هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is accusative under an omitted verb meaning they will be raised that day; God's call commands them to rise for recompense, and their response is accepting it.
rows.anchor: منصوب بفعل مضمر أي تبعثون يوم كذا وكذا والدعوة هي أمره تعالى لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-ḥamdihi is circumstantial: they answer while praising God, since truth will be unveiled and resurrection recognized as a wise and praiseworthy act.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل تستجيبون والتقدير تستجيبون متلبسين بحمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection they will think their stay in the graves was brief; scripture confirms their estimate while correcting their earlier reckoning of its duration.
rows.anchor: تزعمون يوم البعث أنكم لم تلبثوا في القبور بعد الموت إلا زمانا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning a short stay rebukes their impatience and mockery of the delayed Day; their future praise likewise contrasts with present disbelief.
rows.anchor: تعريض لهم في استبطائهم اليوم واستهزائهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants addressed are the believers, with the possessive serving to honor them; the command means to tell them to speak the best word.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بعبادي هم المؤمنون فالإضافة للتشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best expression has gracious manners and avoids harshness, insults, and bad speech.
rows.anchor: أي الكلمه التي هي أحسن، وهو اشتمالها على الأدب الجميل وتعريها عن الخشونة والشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 53–55 form one context: believers must speak graciously and observe manners, remembering that salvation and judgment rest with God, not the Prophet or mere affiliation to him.
rows.anchor: الآية وما بعدها من الآيتين ذات سياق واحد، وخلاصة مضمونها الأمر باحسان القول ولزوم الأدب الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Hijra, believers may have spoken harshly to polytheists and declared them destined for Hell while claiming Paradise for themselves; this provoked hostility and persecution.
rows.anchor: فكان ذلك يهيج المشركين عليهم ويزيد في عداوتهم ويبعثهم إلى المبالغة في فتنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is an order to issue another order; it resembles disputing in the best manner, while Satan's incitement explains the command and his enmity explains the incitement.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأمر، وقوله { إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا } تعليل لنزغ الشيطان بينهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the best saying to mean refraining from fighting the polytheists and dealing peacefully with them; it addresses Meccan believers before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد بقول التي هي أحسن الكف عن قتال المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the peaceful noncombat interpretation because the verse's explanatory context does not fit it.
rows.anchor: وأنت خبير بأن سياق التعليل في الآية لا يلائمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes the opening part of the Prophet's message to believers and its ending a direct address to the Prophet, without a change of speaker; another addresses both Prophet and believers by grammatical predominance.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون الخطاب في صدر الآية للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والمؤمنين جميعا بتغليب جانب خطابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should not speak harshly or pronounce who is saved or damned, since God knows them best and determines who deserves mercy or punishment.
rows.anchor: عليهم أن يرجعوا الأمر ويفوضوه إلى ربهم فربكم - والخطاب للنبي وغيره - أعلم بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy is willed with faith and good works, while punishment is willed with unbelief and disobedience; the Prophet was not appointed to control their fate.
rows.anchor: ولا يشاء ذلك إلا مع الإيمان والعمل الصالح على ما بينه في كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternatives in God's will vary with circumstances of faith, unbelief, and deeds; the verse checks believers from relying on association with the Prophet for salvation.
rows.anchor: أن الترديد في قوله { إن يشأ يرحمكم أو إن يشأ يعذبكم } باعتبار المشيئه المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge of everyone in heaven and earth expands the preceding rationale: He knows the believers better than they know one another.
rows.anchor: صدر الآية توسعة في معنى التعليل السابق كأنه قيل وكيف لا يكون أعلم بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God favored some prophets prepares for David's special favor, the Zabūr, whose praise contains beautiful words about God and encourages gracious speech.
rows.anchor: كأنه تمهيد لقوله { وآتينا داود زبورا } والجملة تذكر فضل داود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī omits other interpretations because they offer no benefit.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية أقوال أخر تركنا التعرض لها لعدم الجدوى

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī explains that if the idols were gods as claimed, they would have ascended to the Throne.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { لو كان معه آلهه كما يقولون إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا } قال قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report means they would seize God's dominion and control affairs; scripture gives no basis for a directional boundary or a vast luminous Throne, neither of which entails divinity.
rows.anchor: أي لاستولوا على ملكه تعالى وأخذوا بأزمة الأمور

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet said Noah, near death, urged his sons to praise God, the prayer of everything by which everything receives provision.
rows.anchor: أخرج أحمد وابن مردويه عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال أن نوحا لما حضرته الوفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The link between universal praise and provision is that each being manifests its need, thereby indicating God's freedom from need.
rows.anchor: فإن الرزق يقدر بالحاجه والسؤال وكل شيء إنما يسبح الله تعالى بالإشاره بإظهار حاجته

rows.speaker: أبو الصباح
rows.claim: Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ reports from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that every thing praises God and that a wall's cracking is its praise; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes another transmission through al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd.
rows.anchor: في تفسير العياشي عن أبي الصباح عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت له قول الله { وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Nawfalī–al-Sakūnī report through Jaʿfar and his father says the Prophet prohibited branding animals and striking their faces because they praise their Lord.
rows.anchor: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يوسم البهائم وأن يضرب وجهها فإنها تسبح بحمد ربها

rows.speaker: محمد بن مسلم
rows.claim: A parallel al-Kāfī report through Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet, forbids striking an animal's face and says not to brand its face.
rows.anchor: وروي النهي عن ضربها على وجوهها الكليني في الكافي بإسناده عن محمد بن مسلم

rows.speaker: إسحاق بن عمار
rows.claim: Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār reports from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that birds and wild animals are caught only when their praise has been neglected.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن إسحاق بن عمار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال ما من طير يصاد في بر أو بحر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The author notes that Sunnis transmit this teaching through Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Abū Hurayra, and others from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى رواه أهل السنة بطرق كثيرة عن ابن مسعود وأبي الدرداء وأبي هريره وغيرهم عن النبي

rows.speaker: مسعدة بن صدقة
rows.claim: Musʿada ibn Ṣadaqa reports from Jaʿfar and his father that dry wood praises God: the cracking sound of house timber is its praise.
rows.anchor: عن مسعده بن صدقة عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عليهما السلام أنه دخل عليه رجل

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said ants praise God.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي هريره أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet prohibited killing frogs because their croaking is praise.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال نهى رسول الله عن قتل الضفدع وقال نعيقها تسبيح

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥamza reports that ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn relayed from his father and ʿAlī that birds praise God and ask for daily sustenance; another version gives this from Muḥammad al-Bāqir.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حمزه قال كنا مع علي بن الحسين فمر بنا عصافير يصحن فقال أتدرون ما تقول هذه العصافير

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet asked her to wash two garments; he explained that a garment praises God and ceases praising when soiled.
rows.anchor: أخرج الخطيب في تاريخه عن عائشة قالت دخل علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال لي

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that animals and small creatures live for the duration of their praise, after which God takes their souls; the report says the Angel of Death has no part.
rows.anchor: أخرج العقيلي في الضعفاء وأبو الشيخ والديلمي عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Angel of Death does not personally take these souls; other angels do so as intermediary causes.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يتصدى بنفسه قبض أرواحها وإنما يباشرها بعض الملائكة والأعوان

rows.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
rows.claim: Muʿādh ibn Anas reports that the Prophet told riders to use mounts gently, not as seats for roadside conversation, since a mount may remember God more than its rider.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ بن أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه مر على قوم وهم وقوف على دواب لهم

rows.speaker: السكوني
rows.claim: Al-Sakūnī reports six rights of a mount from Abū ʿAbd Allāh: do not overburden or sit chatting on it, feed it first, do not brand or strike its face, and offer it water.
rows.anchor: قال للدابة على صاحبها ستة حقوق لا يحملها فوق طاقتها، ولا يتخذ ظهرها مجلسا

rows.speaker: علقمة وابن مسعود
rows.claim: ʿAlqama and Ibn Masʿūd report hearing food praise while the Prophet ate; related reports say pebbles praised in his hand and testified to his prophethood before visitors from Ḥaḍramawt.
rows.anchor: علقمة وابن مسعود كنا نجلس مع النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ونسمع الطعام يسبح

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة وجابر الأنصاري وابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وزين العابدين
rows.claim: These authorities report that a tree trunk groaned when the Prophet moved to a pulpit, then quieted when he embraced it.
rows.anchor: أبو هريرة وجابر الأنصاري وابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وزين العابدين أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يخطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the claim that universal praise consists of human-like audible languages with conventional words hidden from human senses.
rows.anchor: فزعم أن هذا التسبيح العام من قبيل الأصوات، وأن لعامة الأشياء لغة أو لغات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation's praise is literal speech: beings express their Lord's transcendence by manifesting the deficiency of their essences, attributes, and acts while knowing it.
rows.anchor: أن لها تسبيحا هو كلام بحقيقة معنى الكلام وهو إظهارها تنزه ربها بإظهارها نقص ذاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who hear pebbles or mountains praise perceive the real meaning inwardly, which their senses render as suitable words, as abstract realities appear in familiar dream images.
rows.anchor: انما كان بإدراكهم تسبيحها الواقعي بحقيقة معناه من طريق الباطن

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
rows.claim: Asmāʾ reports that when Sūrat al-Masad was revealed, Umm Jamīl arrived denouncing the Prophet with a stone; concealed by Qurʾānic recitation, he was unseen by her, and she asked Abū Bakr whether he had satirized her. Ibn Abī Ḥātim is said to authenticate it.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابو يعلى وابن أبي حاتم وصححه وابن مردويه وأبو نعيم والبيهقي معا في الدلائل عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر

rows.speaker: زرارة
rows.claim: Zurāra reports from one of the two Imams that the basmala is the verse's reference to mentioning God alone; polytheists fled when the Prophet recited it and returned after he finished.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة عن أحدهما عليه السلام قال في { بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم } قال هو أحق ما جهر به

rows.speaker: منصور بن حازم
rows.claim: Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim reports the same explanation of the basmala from Abū ʿAbd Allāh; al-Qummī also transmits it without naming its chain.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا المعنى أيضا عن منصور بن حازم عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام ورواه القمي في تفسيره مضمرا

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī says Quraysh fled when the Prophet loudly recited the basmala at home, linking this to their turning away when God alone is mentioned.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي أنه قال لم كتمتم { بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم } فنعم الاسم

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī reports that Abū Jahl, Abū Sufyān, and al-Akhnas secretly listened to the Prophet's night prayer on three nights, agreed to stop, and reproached one another for risking discovery.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري قال حدثت أن أبا جهل وأبا سفيان والأخنس بن شريق خرجوا ليله يستمعون من رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان
rows.claim: Abū Sufyān said he recognized some of what he heard but not its meaning; Abū Jahl refused belief because prophethood among Banū ʿAbd Manāf threatened their status rivalry.
rows.anchor: قال والله سمعت أشياء أعرفها وأعرف ما يراد بها وسمعت أشياء ما عرفت معناها

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī reports that abused Meccan Muslims asked permission to fight, but the Prophet said no order had come; this was offered as the occasion for the command to speak graciously.
rows.anchor: الآية عن الكلبي. أقول قد أشرنا في تفسير الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the report that this was a command to refrain from fighting does not fit the context.
rows.anchor: أقول قد أشرنا في تفسير الآية أنه لا يلائم سياقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage argues that false gods cannot remove or transfer harm, while those invoked are themselves needy of God; it then explains decreed destruction, withheld signs, and Satan's role in later corruption.
rows.anchor: بيان احتجاج من وجه آخر على التوحيد ونفي ربوبية الآلهة الذين يدعون من دون الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited as saying that every Qurʾānic use of zaʿama refers to a lie.
rows.anchor: ولذا نقل عن ابن عباس أن ما كان في القرآن من الزعم فهو كذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One lexical distinction says nidāʾ requires vocal sound whereas duʿāʾ can be by gesture; another says nidāʾ may stand alone with a call particle while duʿāʾ usually includes the name addressed.
rows.anchor: والدعاء والنداء واحد غير أن النداء إنما هو فيما إذا كان معه صوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A true lord must be able to confer benefit and repel harm, a capacity polytheists seek from their gods; when invoked to remove or transfer harm, these gods cannot do it.
rows.anchor: بأن الرب المستحق للعبادة يجب أن يكون قادرا على إيصال النفع ودفع الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invoked beings are worshiped angels, jinn, and humans; people worship idols to approach them, and celestial worship seeks angelic spirits, while carved material itself is inert.
rows.anchor: فقد بان أولا أن المراد بقوله { الذين زعمتم من دونه } هم الذين كانوا يعبدونهم من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability means lack of independent power without God's aid and permission, as the next verse shows them seeking nearness to Him.
rows.anchor: وثانيا أن المراد بنفي قدرتهم نفي استقلالهم بالقدرة من دون استعانة بالله

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the denial to mean lack of complete power, while granting derivative ability from God; another proposed proof, attributed to al-Ashʿarī, denies their power because all possibilities depend directly on God.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين وكأن المراد من نفي ملكهم ذلك نفي قدرتهم التامة الكاملة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture affirms capacities for angels, jinn, and humans but reserves absolute strength and independent ownership to God; others act only through His empowering and permission.
rows.anchor: غير أنه يخص حقيقه القدرة بنفسه في مثل قوله أن القوة لله جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof cannot deny all capacity to the invoked beings; it denies their independent power, since supplication addresses one who acts independently rather than by another's ownership.
rows.anchor: فلا سبيل إلى تنزيل الحجة في الآية على نفي قدرة آلهتهم من الملائكة والجن والإنس من أصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author introduces an answer to the objection that prayers to idols and to God alike may go unanswered, citing God's promises to answer prayer.
rows.anchor: فقد أجاب الله سبحانه في كلامه عن مثل هذه المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promises apply when a servant earnestly invokes Him without play or attachment to anyone else; at sea, people turn exclusively to God and are rescued.
rows.anchor: وأفاد أن العبد إذا جد بالدعاء ولم يلعب به ولم يتعلق قلبه في دعائه الجدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no parity between unanswered invocation of idols and prayer to God: pagans know that when danger at sea strips away other appeals, God saves them.
rows.anchor: ولم يقابل سبحانه في كلامه بين دعائهم آلهتهم ودعاء المسلمين لإلههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is delivered through the Prophet; if the polytheists objected, he could invoke God sincerely and be answered.
rows.anchor: ومن لطيف النكتة في الكلام إلقاؤه سبحانه الحجة إليهم بواسطة نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, أولئك is the subject, الذين qualifies it, يدعون its relative clause, and يبتغون its predicate; later plural pronouns return to أولئك, and أيهم أقرب explains the search for a means.
rows.anchor: { أولئك } مبتدء و { الذين } صفة له و { يدعون } صلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasīla means approach or that by which one approaches; the latter suits the context of seeking the closest means to God.
rows.anchor: والوسيلة على ما فسروه هي التوصل والتقرب، وربما استعملت بمعنى ما به التوصل والتقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invoked angels, jinn, and humans seek approaches to God and emulate whoever is closest through worshipful works; they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment.
rows.anchor: أولئك الذين يدعوهم المشركون من الملائكة والجن والإنس يطلبون ما يتقربون به إلى ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legitimate seeking nearness through God's close servants preserves worship, hope, and fear directed to God; idolaters instead worship intermediaries as independent powers and approach them through idols and offerings, committing shirk.
rows.anchor: فإنهم يتوسلون إلى الله ويتقربون بالملائكة الكرام والجن والأولياء من الإنس فيتركون عبادته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If أولئك means noble angels, righteous jinn, prophets, and human saints, seeking, hoping, and fearing are literal; if it includes rebellious devils and wicked people such as Pharaoh and Nimrod, these describe creational submission and inherent hope and fear.
rows.anchor: والمراد بأولئك الذين يدعون إن كان هو الملائكة الكرام والصلحاء المقربون من الجن والأنبياء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An alternative takes all pronouns to refer to invoked prophets, who call people to truth or pray to God; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses it as implausible.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن ضمائر الجمع في الآية جميعا راجعة إلى أولئك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers two readings: the invoked gods seek the closest way to God, or they strive through obedience and goodness to be closest; both are acceptable, though the second better fits context.
rows.anchor: وقال في الكشاف في معنى الآية يعني أن آلهتهم أولئك يبتغون الوسيلة وهي القربة إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says those worshipers seek closeness to God by worship, each striving to draw nearest to His mercy; the author says this does not fit the wording.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن معنى الآية أولئك الذين يدعونهم ويعبدونهم ويعتقدون أنهم آلهة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view takes destruction as ordinary death for righteous towns and the severe punishment as extermination for wicked towns.
rows.anchor: ذكروا أن المراد بالعذاب الشديد عذاب الاستئصال فيبقى للإهلاك المقابل له الإماتة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some restrict the towns to unbelieving communities and assign destruction to good towns and punishment to wicked ones; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the restriction has no evidence in context.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المراد بالقرى في الآية القرى الكافرة وأن تعميم القرى لا يساعد عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause means a town's destruction or severe punishment is an inscribed, decisive decree in the Preserved Book.
rows.anchor: أي إهلاك القرى أو تعذيبها عذابا شديدا كان في الكتاب مسطورا وقضاء محتوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prior generations denied signs and were annihilated; their successors are similarly disposed, so demanded signs would destroy them, while God grants respite.
rows.anchor: وقد أرسلناها إلى الأولين فكذبوا بها واستؤصلوا فلو أنا أرسلنا إلى هؤلاء شيئا من جنس تلك الآيات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some explain the verse's connection as an admonition.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكروا في وجه اتصال الآية أنها موعظة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another says it recalls pre-resurrection events to show God's greatness and support what came before.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم كأنه تعالى بعدما ذكر من شأن البعث والتوحيد ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads destruction as extermination and severe punishment as a lesser calamity, such as drought or high prices that drive people away and ruin a town.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالمراد بالإهلاك التدمير بعذاب الاستئصال كما نقل عن أبي مسلم المفسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book records every thing, as the Qurʾān says that everything is enumerated in an imam and that nothing escapes the clear book.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يظهر أن المراد بالكتاب اللوح المحفوظ الذي يذكر القرآن أن الله كتب فيه كل شيء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the Preserved Book details every thing's qualities, causes, and time; objectors argue this requires infinite dimensions, while others propose restricting its scope or compressing its contents potentially, like the jafr.
rows.anchor: وذكر غير واحد أنه ما من شيء إلا بين فيه أي في اللوح المحفوظ والكتاب المسطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the physical-tablet premise: a material tablet could not contain detailed accounts of its own parts, much less all beings and their relations.
rows.anchor: ولو كان كما يقولون لوحا ماديا جسمانيا لم يسع كتابة أسماء أجزائه التي تألف منها جسمه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another position says the finite tablet encompasses infinite things by containing their forms potentially or in summary, comparing it to the comprehensive jafr.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم بالعموم إلا أنه التزم كون البيان على نحو يجتمع مع التناهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān describes the tablet's contents as actual, detailed, and fixed; a material, mutable tablet cannot also be preserved from change, and merely writing the alphabet in a circle would suffice otherwise.
rows.anchor: وكلامه سبحانه فيما يصف فيه هذا اللوح كالصريح أو هو صريح في اشتماله على الأشياء والحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Preserved Book is the totality of existents and events insofar as effects necessarily follow causes, the unalterable decree; “book” and “tablet” are analogies, not a physical object.
rows.anchor: فالحق أن الكتاب المبين هو متن الأعيان بما فيه من الحوادث من جهة ضرورة ترتب المعلولات على عللها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous verse's people inherit corruption and denial, so proposed signs would bring extermination; God withholds them because He does not wish to hasten punishment, and the sūrah later recounts their requests.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الذي منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات التي يقترحونها فإن السابقين منهم اقترحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not literally constrained by an external preventer; “prevented” means sending signs would lack benefit for a people disposed to deny them, whom God chose not to punish immediately.
rows.anchor: فكون تكذيب الأولين لآياته مانعا له من إرسال الآيات المقترحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs' being withheld is explained by the predecessors' denial and the successors' matching disposition; the sūrah appears to have been revealed as one unit.
rows.anchor: وظاهر آيات السورة أنها نزلت دفعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tension between sending signs that would lead to denial and extermination and God's will to give this community respite is expressed metaphorically as prevention; the signs are pictured as ready to descend but held back by corruption.
rows.anchor: عبر عنها في الآية بالمنع استعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling prior nations “the former ones” implies that current people are their successors in nature and conduct, effectively one community; their refrain is recalled at 28:36.
rows.anchor: فيه إيماء إلى أن هؤلاء آخر أولئك الأولين فهم في الحقيقة أمه واحدة لآخرها من الخلق والغريزه ما لأولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested signs were withheld because Quraysh would reject them and deserve extermination as earlier peoples did; this community instead was decreed respite.
rows.anchor: والمقترحون هم قريش - لأنا لو أرسلناها لم يؤمنوا وكذبوا بها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One alternative says requested signs are not sent because God knows the people will not believe, making them pointless; necessary proofs of prophethood and signs that confer grace are still given.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنا لا نرسل الآيات لعلمنا بأنهم لا يؤمنون عندها فيكون إنزالها عبثا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim explains that ancestors requested such signs and did not believe, while their descendants follow them; the author says this view is difficult to distinguish from the preceding account.
rows.anchor: وثانيهما أن المعنى أنا لا نرسل الآيات لأن آباءكم وأسلافكم سألوا مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd were the people of Ṣāliḥ, and the she-camel was a manifest sign; “manifest” can describe the camel or an omitted “sign,” and they wronged themselves by rejecting it.
rows.anchor: ثمود هم قوم صالح ولقد آتاهم الناقه آية، والمبصرة الظاهرة البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs are sent to warn: catastrophic signs threaten destruction in this world and punishment in the next, while other signs warn of afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: أي ان الحكمة في الإرسال بالآيات التخويف والإنذار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further possibility is that lesser calamities induce fear and turn people from worse consequences, as in the cited verse; the author says this reading is plausible.
rows.anchor: وليس من البعيد أن يكون المراد بالتخويف إيجاد الخوف والوحشة بإرسال ما دون عذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four clauses are individually clear but their connection is obscure because the vision and cursed tree are not identified; the cited dreams occur after this Meccan sūrah.
rows.anchor: فقرات الآية وهي أربع واضحة المعاني لكنها بحسب ما بينها من الاتصال وارتباط بعضها ببعض لا تخلد من إجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision is not explained elsewhere; the cursed tree is unidentified in the Qurʾān, which mentions the Zaqqum tree as a trial but never calls it cursed.
rows.anchor: ولا يدرى ما هذه الشجرة الملعونة في القرآن التي جعلها فتنة للناس، ولا توجد في القرآن شجرة يذكرها الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If being a cause of punishment made a tree cursed, Hell and its punishment, its angels, and believers' weapons against unbelievers would also be cursed, though scripture praises the angels.
rows.anchor: لكانت النار وكل ما أعد الله فيها للعذاب ملعونة ولكانت ملائكة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse points back to the ambiguous vision and tree as a trial rather than disclosing exactly what they were; its context links them with rejection of signs and the following Iblīs narrative.
rows.anchor: بل إنما أريدت الإشارة إلى إجمالهما والتذكير بما يقتضيانه بحكم السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier verses describe successive generations rejecting signs and suffering punishment; the following account of Iblīs's temptation of humanity continues that theme.
rows.anchor: المشتملة على قصة إبليس وعجيب تسلطه على إغواء بني آدم تجري على سياق الآيات السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision and cursed tree are matters appearing or present among people that tempt them, spread corruption, and increase tyranny; this is supported by the verse's ending and opening that God encompasses people.
rows.anchor: أن الرؤيا والشجرة المشار إليهما في الآية أمران سيظهران على الناس أو هما ظاهران يفتتن بهما الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān curses Iblīs, Jews, polytheists, hypocrites, and other groups; “tree” can refer to an origin from which branches grow by lineage or adherence.
rows.anchor: وقد لعن في القرآن إبليس ولعن فيه اليهود ولعن فيه المشركون ولعن فيه المنافقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic uses “tree” for a lineage or founding source, as in “from a blessed tree” and the Prophet's saying that he and ʿAlī are from one tree.
rows.anchor: والشجرة كما تطلق على ذي الساق من النبات كذلك تستعمل في الأصل الذي تطلع منه وتنشأ عليه فروع بالنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author excludes identifiable groups among polytheists and People of the Book during the Prophet's time as candidates for this spreading, branching trial.
rows.anchor: ولم يظهر من المشركين وأهل الكتاب في زمن الرسول قبل الهجرة وبعدها قوم بهذا النعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī identifies the cursed tree as hypocrites embedded among Muslims, spreading through descendants or inherited false doctrine and practice; their presence is a trial for the community.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالشجرة الملعونة قوم من المنافقين المتظاهرين بالإسلام يتعرقون بين المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision and tree are linked by God's encompassing people and warnings increasing their tyranny: the verse points to one matter untouched by admonition.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي أن يرتاب في أن في سياق الآية تلويحا بالارتباط بين الفقرتين
